gaps.sentence: The new manager wants to back ___ the sales team's proposal.
gaps.explanation: back up = support (a person, plan); also make a copy of data.

gaps.sentence: They've set ___ a new charity for homeless dogs.
They get ___ on very little money.
gaps.explanation: get by = manage to survive (with difficulty).

gaps.sentence: I stand ___ my decision — it was the right one.
gaps.explanation: stand by something = continue to support it; stand by somebody = help and support them.

gaps.sentence: The chairman walked ___ of the meeting when the press arrived.
gaps.explanation: 'Walk out of' = leave suddenly, often to show disapproval.

gaps.sentence: If you don't know the word, look it ___ in a dictionary.
gaps.explanation: look a word up = find it in a dictionary/reference.

gaps.sentence: These old boots are completely worn ___.
gaps.explanation: wear out = become thin/unusable through use.

gaps.sentence: Don't leave ___ any details in your report.
